text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a weird pattern in snapshot manifests uploaded to s3://redwood-archives this morning. Some objects have an `x-enc-meta` header present but it looks like plaintext JSON (not CMK-encrypted blob). :eyes:
kevin: do you mean the S3 object metadata or the snapshot manifest inside the tar? sample path?
ash: FYI we rolled the backup-uploader role change around 03:10 UTC yesterday as part of the RBAC cleanup. Could be related if creds swapped to a legacy agent.
maria: s3://redwood-archives/db-snap-2026-03-21/manifest.json (I saved a copy). the metadata on the S3 object shows `x-enc-meta: {"cipher":"none","created_by":"backup-agent-v1"}`. looks off.
oliver: can you paste the `aws s3api head-object` output (redact ARNs)? quick check for SSE headers too.
maria: pasted output below:
```
{"ContentLength": 14239817, "Metadata": {"x-enc-meta": "{\"cipher\":\"none\",\"created_by\":\"backup-agent-v1\"}"}, "ServerSideEncryption": "aws:kms", "SSEKMSKeyId": "arn:aws:kms:...:key/..."}
```
kevin: interesting — SSE is KMS but the object-level metadata implies the manifest claims it didn't encrypt payloads. could be a two-step upload: agent uploaded manifest separately from encrypted payloads and the manifest got written without envelope encryption.
ash: timeline: RBAC change removed `backup_uploader:WriteObjectTagging` earlier; I reverted most perms but left a legacy service account bound for a day for canary. agent v1 uses a different upload path that doesn't set envelope metadata correctly.
encops-bot: alert: manifest-not-encrypted pattern matched 8 objects in bucket redwood-archives between 03:05-03:20 UTC. IDs: snap-987, snap-991, snap-997, ...
oliver: good catch. short-term: lock down bucket to deny PutObject without `x-amz-server-side-encryption` and deny PutObject when Metadata.x-enc-meta indicates `cipher":"none"`. can we push an S3 bucket policy?
kevin: policy yes, but we should patch backup-agent to fail manifest writes if it can't confirm envelope metadata. quick fix: add validator that rejects `cipher":"none"` before PutObject. I'll open a patch.
maria: also want an audit query to find any manifests that were later overwritten with `cipher` set to something else (possible remediation attempts). Query logs for PutObject with requester=backup-agent-v1 and metadata.x-enc-meta present.
kevin: creating ticket INFSEC-1427 to track: patch agent, add bucket policy, run inventory, notify customers with affected snapshots. tagging owners: @ash for RBAC audit, @oliver for S3 policy rollout, @maria for incident comms.
ash: noted. I'll run an RBAC diff to ensure no other service accounts have the legacy upload path accidental access.
oliver: I'll stage the bucket policy in prod-readonly and test on staging bucket first. sample policy snippet I'll apply (concept):
```
Effect: Deny
Principal: *
Action: s3:PutObject
Resource: arn:aws:s3:::redwood-archives/*
Condition: StringEqualsIfExists: s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption: "aws:kms"
OR
Condition: ForAnyValue:StringLike: s3:ExistingObjectMetadata.x-enc-meta: "*cipher*:\"none\"*"
```
encops-bot: runbook reminder: if encrypted manifest count > 5 and there are customer-facing snapshots, trigger SEC-Notif workflow and create a P0 if any plaintext data is present.
maria: quick ask — can someone grep S3 access logs for GETs of those manifests? need confirmation whether the manifest content contained anything secret or just metadata.
kevin: I'll run the grep and post findings. if manifests only include pointers and not keys/credentials then severity remains medium; otherwise escalate.
maria: thanks team. will draft a short customer note template in INFSEC-1427 once we know scope. :thumbsup:
